nodes.description: The p.Leu335Pro substitution lies close to the hydrophobic sleeve of the alpha3beta3 hexamer that grips the tip of the rotating gamma subunit. Proline substitution at this conserved position is proposed to loosen the contact between the beta subunit and the gamma stalk. The mutant protein is expressed at somewhat lower levels than wild type but still assembles into macromolecular complex V, so the lesion is a functional one at an intersubunit interface rather than a failure of assembly.

nodes.description: Protons continue to pass through the FO pore and drive stalk rotation, but the mechanical energy is no longer efficiently captured as ATP. The proton motive force is therefore dissipated without a matching rise in ATP synthesis, and the lost energy appears as heat. Pharmacological silencing of complex V with oligomycin abolishes the excess leak, and maximal stimulation with saturating ADP also removes the difference from control, which localises the defect to complex V itself rather than to a leaky inner membrane.

nodes.description: Because the proton gradient is continuously dissipated, the respiratory chain runs faster to rebuild it. Basal oxygen consumption is elevated in intact and permeabilized patient fibroblasts and in engineered mutant cells. This is the inverse of the depressed respiration that characterises most mitochondrial disease.

nodes.description: The inner membrane potential, which is the dominant component of the proton motive force in human mitochondria, is reduced after glutamate and malate addition in a line derived from Patient 2, and at baseline in the isogenic CRISPR knock-in clones. Two controls localise the leak to complex V: the depolarization is corrected by oligomycin, and potential following ADP addition is comparable to control, so the difference disappears when the enzyme is either silenced or maximally stimulated.

nodes.description: Energy from oxidised substrate that is not captured as ATP leaves the system as heat. This is the proposed basis of the patients' hyperthermia and diaphoresis, although the authors note it does not explain why the hyperthermia is episodic rather than continuous.

At the whole-organism level the uncoupling appears as euthyroid hypermetabolism: caloric intake several times the estimated resting energy expenditure, without weight gain. Thyroid function is normal, which separates this from the far commoner endocrine causes of hypermetabolism.

nodes.description: NM_001686.3:c.1004T>C, p.(Leu335Pro). De novo and heterozygous in both twins. Leu335 sits near the hydrophobic sleeve of the alpha3beta3 hexamer that holds the gamma stalk tip, and is close to several yeast mgi residues whose mutation uncouples respiration from ATP synthesis. The authors propose it is the human equivalent of a yeast group 1 mgi mutation, impairing engagement of the gamma subunit by the hexamer. The functional consequence is dominant-negative on coupling rather than a loss of catalytic activity.
